overview.headline: Wright brothers early lift equation and flight testing

keyPoints.point: Wright brothers understood lift must overcome weight of aircraft
keyPoints.quote: They knew that they needed to generate enough aerodynamic lift to overcome the weight of their aircraft.

keyPoints.point: Lift generation depends on air properties, velocity, surface area, shape and inclination called angle of attack
keyPoints.quote: The amount of lift generated by an object depends on a number of factors, including properties of the air, the velocity between the object and the air

keyPoints.point: Early studies showed lift varies with square of velocity and linearly with surface area
keyPoints.quote: it had been determined that lift depends on the square of the velocity and varies linearly with the surface area of the object.

keyPoints.point: The 1900s equation defines lift as Smeaton coefficient times velocity squared times wing area times lift coefficient
keyPoints.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: fraction of pressure force converted into lift representing shape and inclination effects
keyTerms.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure coefficient representing force on flat plate moving through air
keyTerms.quote: Early aerodynamicists characterized the dependence on the properties of the air by a pressure coefficient called Smeaton’s coefficient

keyTerms.gloss: inclination of body relative to airflow affecting lift generation
keyTerms.quote: the body’s inclination to the flow, also called the angle of attack.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure due to moving air used in modern lift formulation
keyTerms.quote: The modern equation uses the dynamic pressure of the moving air for the pressure dependence, while this equation uses the Smeaton coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: surface area of wing over which air flows to generate lift
keyTerms.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.
